messages.subject: Rotate specimens
parts:
Dear all,

I realise this is not, strictly speaking, a Geomorph related question. But I hope that some of you might be able to point me in the right direction.

I study differences in floral shape across Pelargonium (Geraniaceae) species. As a result of digitising, not all my specimens are in the same orientation which should normally not be a problem because this is 'fixed' in the Procrust analysis. However, for an exploratory step, I would like to be able to orient all my specimens in the same way without removing the size component. For example, I have an individual oriented like the first picture (Capture1, with the stem oriented to the top left corner), while the majority of my specimens is oriented like the second picture (Capture2, with the stem horizontally). I would like to be able to orient all my specimens with their stem in a horizontal way, as in Capture2. There are many different ways the orientation of specimens differs (some are more angled towards the top, others to the bottom), so I cannot perform a matrix transformation of a standard number of degrees.

To start, I have tried to use the 'fixed.angle' command in Geomorph to rotate my specimens, since I can define a hingepoint but it is not working entirely correct yet. I was hoping maybe someone could give me any tips or has done this before?

Thanks in advance!

Regards,
Sara

messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Rotate specimens
parts:
Sara,

 

If you wish to orient them after digitizing, one can do that in two steps in geomorph. First, perform a GPA, second put the size component back in. Example below.

 

Dean

 

##

library(geomorph)

data(plethodon)

Y.gpa <- gpagen(plethodon$land)

size.shape <- simplify2array(lapply(1:dim(plethodon$land)[3], function(j) Y.gpa$coords[,,j] * Y.gpa$Csize[[j]]) )

 

#check

plotAllSpecimens(Y.gpa$coords)

plotAllSpecimens(size.shape)

Dear all,

 

I realise this is not, strictly speaking, a Geomorph related question. But I hope that some of you might be able to point me in the right direction.

 

I study differences in floral shape across Pelargonium (Geraniaceae) species. As a result of digitising, not all my specimens are in the same orientation which should normally not be a problem because this is 'fixed' in the Procrust analysis. However, for an exploratory step, I would like to be able to orient all my specimens in the same way without removing the size component. For example, I have an individual oriented like the first picture (Capture1, with the stem oriented to the top left corner), while the majority of my specimens is oriented like the second picture (Capture2, with the stem horizontally). I would like to be able to orient all my specimens with their stem in a horizontal way, as in Capture2. There are many different ways the orientation of specimens differs (some are more angled towards the top, others to the bottom), so I cannot perform a matrix transformation of a standard number of degrees.

 

To start, I have tried to use the 'fixed.angle' command in Geomorph to rotate my specimens, since I can define a hingepoint but it is not working entirely correct yet. I was hoping maybe someone could give me any tips or has done this before?

 

Thanks in advance!

 

Regards,

Sara

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Rotate specimens
parts:
Hi Sara, 

I wrote an R function a few years ago that does what you are asking for 3D data with more than 1 midline landmark (it actually may require more than 2... can't remember). 

The function, preferred.rotation, is here: https://gist.github.com/davidckatz/3812f9270991b09eef3a1cd45913d3e1

Basically, the function aligns the configuration of interest to Cartesian x, y, z axes. You have to select landmarks that serve as guidepoints for the alignment. Could be buggy, or not work on all data, but regardless the operations within the function may be something you can build on. The function is pretty decently commented.

You can generate a rotation for one configuration (e.g., a mean) and rotate the rest of your superimposed specimens with that rotation matrix. Or you can rotate each individual. Up to you.

Good luck, David
PS if you try it, I'd be interested to hear back from you, succeed or fail.

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Rotate specimens
parts:
Hi Sara,

Right, 2D v 3D. As long as you have midlines (or some other subset of landmarks whose deviations you want to minimize with respect to an axis), I think with 2D data you can simply do this:

For a single specimen:
d1 <- [p*2 matrix of coordinate or post-GPA data for one specimen]
midlines <- [index of the rows of d1 that contain midline landmarks]
d1.aligned <- d1%*%eigen(var(d1[midlines,]))$vectors

If you instead have "d", a p*k*n array, you can build a loop to apply the transformation to each observation. You'd create an empty array d.aligned, with dimensions the same as d. In this case, the last line would change to:
for(i in 1:n){d.aligned[,,i] <- d%*%eigen(var(d[midlines,,i]))$vectors}

You might get some unwanted reflections, but if your goal is simply to have easy viewing, maybe that doesn't matter. If it's a problem, the code to prevent reflection in 3D is heading #2 in the github code. Play around with it a little and I bet you'll be able to figure out the 2D version. Or write back and I'll play around with it.

David

Dear all,

I realise this is not, strictly speaking, a Geomorph related question. But I hope that some of you might be able to point me in the right direction.

I study differences in floral shape across Pelargonium (Geraniaceae) species. As a result of digitising, not all my specimens are in the same orientation which should normally not be a problem because this is 'fixed' in the Procrust analysis. However, for an exploratory step, I would like to be able to orient all my specimens in the same way without removing the size component. For example, I have an individual oriented like the first picture (Capture1, with the stem oriented to the top left corner), while the majority of my specimens is oriented like the second picture (Capture2, with the stem horizontally). I would like to be able to orient all my specimens with their stem in a horizontal way, as in Capture2. There are many different ways the orientation of specimens differs (some are more angled towards the top, others to the bottom), so I cannot perform a matrix transformation of a standard number of degrees.

To start, I have tried to use the 'fixed.angle' command in Geomorph to rotate my specimens, since I can define a hingepoint but it is not working entirely correct yet. I was hoping maybe someone could give me any tips or has done this before?
